'''Robert C. Duncan (Jr.)''' (born September 2, 1955) is an American astrophysicist now retired from the [[University of Texas at Austin]].

Duncan was born in [[Pensacola, Florida]], in 1955.  He grew up in Houston and Boston, where his father played a key role in NASA's Apollo Project.<ref>[https://nap.nationalacademies.org/read/11912/chapter/19 Robert C. Duncan | Memorial Tributes: Volume 11 |The National Academies Press]</ref>  Duncan (Jr.) later earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in physics from [[Dartmouth College]] in 1977 and a PhD in physics from [[Cornell University]] in 1986.  He also studied at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Duncan |first=Robert Clifton |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=21pUAAAAYAAJ&q=robert+c.+duncan+cornell+dartmouth+astrophysics |title=Topics in the Theory of Neutron Star Cooling |date=1986 |publisher=Cornell University |language=en}}</ref>  As a student, Duncan was a competitive runner<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-08-26 |title=1976 |url=https://hepstrack.wordpress.com/heps-cross-country/mens-results/the-1970s/1976-2/ |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=HepsTrack.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Auran |first=James D. |title=Dartmouth Outdistances Harriers, 25-30 {{!}} News {{!}} The Harvard Crimson |url=https://api.thecrimson.com/article/1976/10/16/dartmouth-outdistances-harriers-25-30-ptwo-crimson/ |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=api.thecrimson.com |language=en}}</ref> and marathoner.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ARRS - Runner: Robert C Duncan |url=https://more.arrs.run/runner/15104 |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=more.arrs.run}}</ref>

From 1986 to 1988, Duncan worked as a postdoctoral researcher at [[Princeton University]]. With [[Christopher Thompson (astronomer)|Christopher Thompson]], he proposed and developed the theory of [[magnetar]]s,<ref>{{cite journal |author=Robert C. Duncan |author2=Christopher Thompson |name-list-style=amp |date=June 10, 1992 |title=Formation of Very Strongly Magnetized Neutron Stars: Implications for Gamma-Ray Bursts |url=http://adsbit.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/nph-iarticle_query?bibcode=1992ApJ...392L...9D |journal=Astronomical Journal |volume=392 |issue=1 |pages=L9–L13 |bibcode=1992ApJ...392L...9D |doi=10.1086/186413|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Duncan |first1=Robert C. |last2=Thompson |first2=Christopher |title=AIP Conference Proceedings |date=1996-04-01 |chapter=Magnetars |journal=High Velocity Neutron Stars |chapter-url=https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1996AIPC..366..111D |volume=366 |pages=111–117 |doi=10.1063/1.50235|bibcode=1996AIPC..366..111D }}</ref> and was awarded the [[Bruno Rossi Prize]] for this work in 2003.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rossi Prize Winners 2003: Robert Duncan, Christopher Thompson, & Chryssa Kouveliotou |url=http://www.aas.org/head/rossi/rossi.recip.html#S |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080406082614/http://www.aas.org/head/rossi/rossi.recip.html#S |archivedate=2008-04-06 |publisher=[[High Energy Astrophysics Division]] of the [[American Astronomical Society]]}}</ref> Duncan has written scientific research papers about [[neutron star]]s, [[supernova]]e, intergalactic [[gas cloud]]s, [[neutrino]] emissions of very dense matter and related topics.<ref>[https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/search/fq=%7B!type%3Daqp%20v%3D%24fq_database%7D&fq_database=database%3A%20astronomy&q=author%3A(%22Duncan%2C%20Robert%20C.%22)&sort=citation_count%20desc%2C%20bibcode%20desc&p_=0 Duncan, Robert C.  NASA Astrophysics Data System, Citation-ranked list]</ref>
